acceptanceCriteria.notes: ⚠️ Written BEFORE the code, unlike ACC-0001..0009. `not-evaluated` is the honest state and is exactly the distinction QST-0015 was about: the criterion exists, the work does not. ⚠️ EVALUATED 2026-08-22: `test/handoff.test.mjs` covers it in four parts — a slice carries its tasks' requirements, criteria and components; a cross-role dependency is visible to the blocked role; no tasks means no slices; and slugs are stable. ⚠️ The cross-role case is covered by a CONSTRUCTED fixture, because this project has exactly one role — so the case the criterion is really about has been tested but not lived.
acceptanceCriteria.statement: For each role in the task graph, the generated slice contains every task assigned to that role together with the requirements and acceptance criteria those tasks trace to, and nothing is a reference to a file outside the package.
acceptanceCriteria.title: Every role slice is self-sufficient

components.responsibility: Checks storage identity, trace integrity, content completeness, lifecycle and instruction safety across all artifacts, and blocks at the two boundaries #46 names.
components.title: The lint

components.notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT — 2026-08-22. This is the first component designed BEFORE it exists rather than recorded after; every other CMP describes a module already on disk. `implementedBy` is absent for exactly that reason, and its absence is the only signal in the artifact that says so. ⚠️ THE HAZARD THIS CREATES IS REAL AND IS RAISED AS QST-0015: the orphan check counts EDGES, so creating this record takes the orphan count to zero while REQ-0010 remains unimplemented. 'All requirements trace to a component' becomes true; 'the handoff exists' does not. A correct rule producing an invisible outcome is the pattern #94, #107 and #122 all describe, and the attestation carries the distinction until something better does. ⚠️ Design decided in DEC-0009: an explicit deterministic command (`npm run handoff`), NEVER a gate side effect. The gate stays read-only. ⚠️ IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-22 — and `implementedBy` now pointing somewhere proves CODE EXISTS, not that the component satisfies its acceptance criteria. QST-0015 stays open for exactly that reason: a path is not a verdict, and nothing here has yet been judged against criteria nobody has written (stage 7's job). ⚠️ The command REFUSES this project today, by design: stage 5's third criterion is attested not-satisfied, so `npm run handoff` reports 11 blockers and writes nothing.
components.responsibility: Produce the frozen handoff package under docs/plan/ from planning-content, on an explicit deterministic command, such that a recipient can begin their part of the work without asking the planner for information the plan should already contain.
components.title: Handoff export

note: Generated as a query over the task graph, grouped by `task.role` (#19). Nothing here is authored: re-running the handoff recomputes it, so a slice cannot drift from the plan.

requirements.rationale: Intake: 'the runbook should represent the output of discovery, not the beginning of discovery.'
requirements.statement: No instruction in the final output may rest on a claim whose basis is below the level required for that instruction.
requirements.title: Instructions rest on resolved claims

requirements.rationale: Intake objective, stated in the PM's own terms.
requirements.statement: A recipient of the output must be able to begin their part of the work without asking the planner for information the plan should have contained.
requirements.title: The handoff is actionable without returning to the planner

requirements.rationale: Intake stakeholders: the material explicitly declines to assume which the implementer is. This is testable by comparing both consumers against the same required-information inventory.
requirements.statement: For every required item in the handoff, both a human reader and an automated consumer must be able to recover the same information without depending on the other representation.
requirements.title: The output serves a human or an agent implementer

tasks.statement: Extend the handoff renderer to emit one slice per role, as a query over tasks grouped by `role`, pulling each task's traced requirements and acceptance criteria with it. No slice is authored or maintained.
tasks.title: Generate role slices from the task graph

tasks.statement: Replace `load-bearing-assertions-at-rung`'s reliance on the optional `loadBearing` flag with a scope derived from the graph — at minimum, every assertion referenced by an active runbook step's `restsOn`.
tasks.title: Derive stage 6's scope from graph use rather than a flag
